newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Gas debts mean Kazakhs face bleak winter.
newsitem.headline: Gas debts mean Kazakhs face bleak winter.

text.p: Some inhabitants of the snow-covered Kazakh captial Almaty had to heat water on fires in the street on Wednesday after neighbouring former Soviet republic Uzbekistan shut off gas supplies.
Uzbekistan has cut supplies of natural gas because Kazakhstan has failed to pay $26 million in debts, Kazakh Deputy Oil and Gas Minister Anatoly Lobaev told Reuters.
Most homes in Almaty, located at the foot of the spectacular Tien Shan mountains in the depths of Central Asia, have had no gas for nearly a week.
Commercial television showed inhabitants boiling water on fires outside their homes as temperatures dropped to minus three degrees Celsius (26.6 Fahrenheit).
Ironically, the shortages come as western investors flock to the vast republic in the hope of exploiting its own rich reserves of oil and gas.
Gas has also been cut to the major Kazakh towns of Chimkent and Dzhambul where temperatures on the bleak, empty steppe often drop to minus 40C (minus 40F) in winter.
